walkthroughs.body_html:
Property depends on what you must break to melt or dissolve it.

Ionic: high mp, conducts when molten or dissolved.

Simple molecular: low mp, does not conduct.

Diamond: each C bonded to 4 others - very hard, no free electrons.

Graphite: each C bonded to 3 others; free electron per atom -> conducts.

Graphene: a single layer of graphite - strong and conducting.

Polymers are long chains of repeating units joined by covalent bonds.

Forces between chains are strong compared to small molecules, so mp is higher.

Alloys are mixtures - different sized atoms stop layers sliding, so harder than pure metal.

options: ions are charged only when molten
ions are free to move when molten
it gains electrons

mcqs.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity but diamond does not?
options: Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.
Graphite has delocalised electrons between layers; diamond has all four outer electrons in localised covalent bonds.
Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.
Graphite conducts because it is a metal, while diamond is a non-metal.

mcqs.q: When water boils, what is broken?
options: Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.
The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.
Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.
Delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice of positive ions, carrying charge.
Metal atoms themselves move to carry the current.
